title: Well Control Method Statement
description: Free Well Control Method Statement template for oil & gas you can edit online and download as PDF. Covers well information, 3.0 bop equipment specification, 4.0 bop testing procedure.
standard: API RP 59 / API RP 53 / IADC Well Control Manual

Well Information

METHOD STATEMENT ID: WC-MS-__________ DATE: ______________ REVISION: ______________

WELL NAME: ______________ RIG #: ______________ FIELD: ______________

OPERATOR: ______________ CONTRACTOR: ______________ TOOLPUSHER: ______________

1.0 SCOPE: This procedure covers well control equipment, testing, and response during drilling operations.

2.0 RESPONSIBILITIES:

• Toolpusher: Overall well control readiness • Driller: Primary well control monitoring

• Company Man: Critical decisions during kick • All Crew: Trained in well control procedures

3.0 Bop Equipment Specification

COMPONENT SIZE PRESSURE RATING QUANTITY FUNCTION

Annular BOP _________" _____________ psi _____ Seal any size pipe

Pipe Rams _________" _____________ psi _____ Seal around drill pipe

Blind/Shear Rams _________" _____________ psi _____ Shear pipe & seal well

Variable Bore Rams _________" _____________ psi _____ Accommodate different pipe sizes

Choke Manifold _________" _____________ psi _____ Control flow during kill

Kill Manifold _________" _____________ psi _____ Pump into well

Accumulator Unit ________gal _____________ psi _____ Operate BOPs

4.0 Bop Testing Procedure

4.1 Pressure Test Schedule:

• Low pressure test: 200-300 psi (every ________ days)

• High pressure test: _____________ psi (every ________ days)

• Function test: _____________ days

• After any BOP repair or modification

4.2 Test Sequence:

Step 1: Notify all personnel of BOP testing

Step 2: Secure well and position test plug/ cup

Step 3: Test annular BOP (low then high pressure)

Step 4: Test pipe rams (low then high pressure)

Step 5: Test blind/shear rams (low then high pressure)

Step 6: Test choke and kill lines

Step 7: Document all test results

Step 8: Post-test meeting and sign-off

4.3 Acceptance Criteria:

• Pressure stable for 5 minutes

• Drop < 10% of test pressure

• No visible leaks

• Rams function properly

5.0 Primary Well Control (Mud)

5.1 Mud Parameters:

• Current mud weight: _____________ ppg (range: _____________ - _____________ ppg)

• Mud type: _____________ (water-based / oil-based / synthetic)

• Pit volume: _____________ bbl (high alarm at _____________ bbl)

• Flow show: monitored continuously

• Trip tank: _____________ bbl (monitored during trips)

5.2 Kick Indicators:

PRIMARY INDICATORS: SECONDARY INDICATORS:

• Flow increase with pumps off • Drilling break

• Pit volume increase • Increase in ROP

• Flowing well with pumps off • Torque increase

• Pump pressure changes

• Gas cutting of mud

6.0 Shut-In Procedure (Hard Shut-In)

UPON DETECTING A KICK:

1. Pick up kelly/ top drive to clear rotary table

2. Stop rotary and pumps

3. Check for flow - if flow continues:

a. Open hydraulic valve on HCR (if equipped)

b. Close annular BOP or pipe rams

c. Close choke (if open)

d. Check for well shut-in (flow stopped)

e. Record SIDPP and SICP immediately

f. Record pit gain

4. Inform Company Man and Toolpusher

5. Prepare for kill operation

7.0 Kill Procedures

7.1 Driller's Method:

• First circulation: Circulate kick out using original mud weight

- Maintain _____________ psi casing pressure

- Pump at _____________ spm (_____________ bpm)

- Monitor gas at choke

• Second circulation: Kill well with heavier mud

- Kill mud weight: _____________ ppg

- Pump kill mud at _____________ bpm

- Maintain _____________ psi drill pipe pressure

- Stop when kill mud at bit and circulating

7.2 Wait and Weight Method:

• Calculate kill mud weight: _____________ ppg

• Mix kill mud while waiting

• Pump kill mud in one circulation

• Maintain _____________ psi drill pipe pressure schedule

• Stop when kill mud at surface

8.0 Tripping Procedures

8.1 Trip Sheet Requirements:

• Record pipe pulled/ run each stand

• Calculate displacement each stand

• Compare actual vs calculated pit volume

• If difference > _____________ bbl, flow check

8.2 Trip Tank Monitoring:

• Monitor trip tank continuously

• Trip tank volume: _____________ bbl

• Allowable gain/loss per stand: _____________ bbl

• Flow check if outside limits

8.3 Tripping Practices:

• Slow circulation rate when pulling out of hole

• Maintain hole full at all times

• Use mud saver valve

• Break circulation at regular intervals

9.0 Stripping And Snubbing Procedures

• Ensure BOP rams sized for pipe being stripped

• Maintain _____________ psi below annular BOP

• Monitor pipe position continuously

• Strip at controlled speed (max _____________ ft/min)

• Use pipe wipers to prevent mud loss

10.0 Volumetric Control Procedure

• Used when unable to circulate (gas migration)

• Allow gas to expand at controlled rate

• Bleed mud at calculated intervals

• Maintain casing pressure within _____________ - _____________ psi

• Continue until gas at surface

11.0 Bullheading Procedure

• Pump kill fluid down drill pipe and annulus

• Ensure formation fracture pressure not exceeded

• Pump rate: _____________ bpm

• Max pressure: _____________ psi

• Monitor for formation breakdown

12.0 Well Control Drills

12.1 Drill Schedule:

• Weekly well control drill (all crews)

• Monthly BOP function test drill

• Quarterly simulated kick drill

• Annual full-scale exercise

12.2 Drill Requirements:

• Time to shut-in: target < 3 minutes

• All crew members participate

• Record response times

• Debrief after each drill

• Document in drilling report

14.0 Emergency Procedures

LOSS OF WELL CONTROL:

1. Activate emergency alarm

2. Shut down all non-essential equipment

3. Evacuate non-essential personnel

4. Activate emergency response plan

5. Notify operator and authorities

6. Prepare for possible relief well
